New Tree Requests can be made via the 311 app, by calling 311, or by contacting the Urban Forestry Division by sending an email to trees@boston.gov or calling 617-635-8733. The best way to get information about Boston's street trees is by going to boston.gov/trees and reading about how to properly request a new street tree, to submit tree maintenance requests, and learn how to care for young street trees. We understand and appreciate why seeing the flag flown at half-mast in a timely manner is important, especially during moments of remembrance and respect. Thank you for contacting us regarding the irrigation system and the second watering cycle that occurs around noon. The midday irrigation cycle is intentional and is used only during periods of prolonged heat or unusually dry conditions (June - August). Rather than serving as a full watering, this shorter cycle supplements the early morning irrigation by helping maintain adequate soil moisture and reducing stress on the turf during the hottest part of the day. This is particularly important for recently established turf and heavily used lawn areas. While early morning remains the primary watering time, the additional midday cycle is a temporary measure used to protect the health of the lawn during extreme weather conditions. Once temperatures moderate, the irrigation schedule is adjusted and the supplemental midday watering is discontinued. We appreciate your understanding as we work to maintain healthy, safe, and resilient park landscapes during periods of extreme heat. Sincerely, Boston Parks and Recreation Department
